cards.name: Frontal belly of occipitofrontalis (frontalis)
cards.function: Anterior belly of the scalp muscle; it has no bony attachment and raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead horizontally.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Epicranial aponeurosis at the level of the coronal suture

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the frontal region and eyebrows (blending with procerus, corrugator supercilii and orbicularis oculi)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery (with supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries)

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the skin of the forehead horizontally

cards.pearl: Forehead sparing marks an upper motor neuron facial palsy, because the part of the facial nucleus supplying frontalis receives bilateral cortical input; in Bell palsy the forehead cannot wrinkle.

cards.name: Occipital belly of occipitofrontalis (occipitalis)
cards.function: Posterior belly of the scalp muscle; it pulls the scalp backward and anchors the epicranial aponeurosis so the frontal belly can lift the brows.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lateral two-thirds of the superior nuchal line and the mastoid process

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Epicranial aponeurosis and skin of the occipital region

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior auricular nerve (branch of CN VII)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital branch of posterior auricular artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Moves the scalp backward and fixes the epicranial aponeurosis

cards.pearl: The posterior auricular nerve leaves CN VII just below the stylomastoid foramen, so the occipital belly is spared by lesions of the facial nerve within the parotid gland.

cards.name: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica)
cards.function: Tough tendinous sheet over the calvaria that joins the frontal and occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis and forms the third layer of the scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis posteriorly; superior nuchal line and external occipital protuberance between them

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Frontal bellies of occipitofrontalis anteriorly; continuous laterally with the temporal fascia, where auricularis anterior and superior arise

details.label: Innervation
details.value: None of its own (its muscle bellies are supplied by CN VII)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Scalp arteries run in the dense connective tissue superficial to it

details.label: Action
details.value: Transmits the pull of the frontal and occipital bellies; moves with the skin as one unit over the loose areolar layer

cards.pearl: A scalp wound that divides the aponeurosis coronally gapes widely because the two bellies pull the edges apart; the loose areolar layer beneath it is the danger area, through which blood and infection spread to the eyelids and via emissary veins to the cranial cavity.

cards.name: Orbital part of orbicularis oculi
cards.function: Thick outer ring of the eyelid sphincter that surrounds the orbital margin and screws the eyes tightly shut.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial orbital margin (nasal part of frontal bone, frontal process of maxilla) and medial palpebral ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Fibers loop around the orbit without interruption and return to the medial palpebral ligament; skin around the orbit

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal and zygomatic branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Facial and superficial temporal arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Forceful (voluntary) closure of the eyelids; draws the brow and cheek skin toward the eye

cards.pearl: Squeezing the eyes shut against resistance tests it; its contraction produces the lateral 'crow's feet' wrinkles treated with botulinum toxin.

cards.name: Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi
cards.function: Thin inner part of the eyelid sphincter lying within the lids in front of the orbital septum and tarsi; closes the lids gently in blinking and sleep.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial palpebral ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral palpebral ligament (raphe), arching across both eyelids anterior to the tarsi

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Zygomatic (and temporal) branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Facial and superficial temporal arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Gentle and reflex closure of the eyelids (blink); spreads the tear film and holds the lower lid against the globe

cards.pearl: Paralysis in CN VII palsy causes lagophthalmos with exposure keratitis, and the unsupported lower lid falls away from the globe (paralytic ectropion) so tears spill over (epiphora).

cards.name: Superficial part of masseter
cards.function: Larger, anterior part of masseter whose fibers slope downward and backward; it elevates the mandible and helps protrude it.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic arch: maxillary process of the zygomatic bone and anterior two-thirds of the lower border of the arch

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Angle and lower lateral surface of the ramus of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Masseteric nerve (CN V3, anterior division)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and protrudes the mandible

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Transverse facial artery; masseteric branch of maxillary artery and branches of facial artery

cards.pearl: Palpated over the angle of the mandible during jaw clenching to test the motor root of CN V; the parotid duct crosses its surface and turns medially at its anterior border.

cards.name: Deep part of masseter
cards.function: Smaller, posterior part of masseter with vertical fibers hidden by the superficial part; it elevates the mandible and its fibers retract it.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic arch: medial surface and posterior third of the lower border

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper lateral surface of the ramus and the coronoid process of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Masseteric nerve (CN V3, anterior division), entering its deep surface through the mandibular notch

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates the mandible; deep fibers retract it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Masseteric branch of maxillary artery; transverse facial artery

cards.pearl: The masseteric nerve and artery reach the muscle through the mandibular notch on its deep surface, so the superficial surface can be dissected without denervating it.

cards.name: Superior head of lateral pterygoid
cards.function: Smaller upper head of lateral pterygoid; it attaches to the capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint and controls the disc as the jaw closes.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Infratemporal surface (and crest) of the greater wing of the sphenoid bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint, and the pterygoid fovea

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Mandibular nerve (CN V3), nerve to lateral pterygoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular (pterygoid) branches of maxillary artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Draws the articular disc forward with the condyle in protrusion and steadies the disc as it returns during closing

cards.pearl: Spasm or incoordination of this head is implicated in anterior disc displacement, producing the click of temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

cards.name: Inferior head of lateral pterygoid
cards.function: Larger lower head of lateral pterygoid; it pulls the condyle forward onto the articular tubercle to protrude the mandible and open the mouth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the condylar process of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Mandibular nerve (CN V3), nerve to lateral pterygoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular (pterygoid) branches of maxillary artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Bilaterally protrudes the mandible and opens the mouth; unilaterally swings the jaw to the opposite side for grinding

cards.pearl: With a unilateral CN V3 lesion the jaw deviates toward the paralyzed side on opening, pushed across by the intact opposite muscle; the buccal nerve emerges between the two heads and the maxillary artery usually passes between or superficial to them.

cards.name: Anterior belly of digastric
cards.function: First pharyngeal arch belly of digastric in the floor of the mouth; with the mylohyoid it depresses the mandible and raises the hyoid, and it separates the submental from the submandibular triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Digastric fossa of the mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Intermediate tendon, slung to the body of the hyoid bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to mylohyoid (from the inferior alveolar nerve, CN V3)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Branches of the submental artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the hyoid bone and base of the tongue; opens the mouth by lowering the mandible when the hyoid is fixed

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies on mylohyoid; the two anterior bellies and the hyoid bound the submental triangle; forms the anterior boundary of the submandibular triangle

cards.pearl: The two bellies have different nerves because of different arch origins: anterior belly from the 1st arch (CN V3 via nerve to mylohyoid), posterior belly from the 2nd arch (CN VII).

cards.name: Posterior belly of digastric
cards.function: Second pharyngeal arch belly of digastric running from the mastoid to the hyoid; it elevates and retracts the hyoid and is the key surgical landmark of the upper neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Intermediate tendon, slung to the body of the hyoid bone (it pierces the stylohyoid tendon)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Facial nerve (digastric branch, given off just below the stylomastoid foramen)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the posterior auricular and occipital arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and steadies the hyoid bone during swallowing; assists in opening the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses superficial to the internal jugular vein, internal and external carotid arteries, and CN X, XI and XII; forms the posterior boundary of the submandibular triangle and the upper boundary of the carotid triangle

cards.pearl: Surgeons call it the 'resident's friend': everything important in the upper neck (internal jugular vein, carotids, CN X, XI, XII) lies deep to it, and in parotid surgery the facial nerve trunk is found just above its upper border.

cards.name: Straight part of cricothyroid
cards.function: Anterior, nearly vertical part of cricothyroid; it pulls the thyroid cartilage down toward the cricoid arch, tilting it forward to lengthen and tense the vocal ligaments.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior border of the lamina of the thyroid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (cricothyroid branch of superior thyroid)

details.label: Action
details.value: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward and down at the cricothyroid joints, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments (raises pitch)

details.label: Relations
details.value: The two straight parts flank the median cricothyroid ligament, the site of emergency cricothyrotomy

cards.pearl: External laryngeal nerve injury during ligation of the superior thyroid artery paralyzes cricothyroid: a weak, easily fatigued voice that cannot reach high pitch.

cards.name: Oblique part of cricothyroid
cards.function: Posterior part of cricothyroid whose fibers run backward to the inferior horn; it draws the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage (behind the straight part)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage and adjacent lower border of the lamina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Glides the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid at the cricothyroid joints, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies just in front of the cricothyroid joint, behind which the recurrent laryngeal nerve enters the larynx; overlapped by sternothyroid

cards.name: Transverse arytenoid
cards.function: The only unpaired intrinsic laryngeal muscle; it bridges the two arytenoid cartilages and pulls them together to close the posterior, intercartilaginous part of the rima glottidis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface and lateral border of one arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Corresponding surface of the opposite arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (both sides)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (laryngeal branches)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts the arytenoid cartilages, closing the intercartilaginous portion of the rima glottidis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to the oblique arytenoids; covered posteriorly by the mucosa of the laryngopharynx

cards.pearl: Because it is a single midline muscle supplied from both sides, it keeps working after a unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve lesion.

cards.name: Oblique arytenoid
cards.function: Paired bundles that cross like an X on the back of the transverse arytenoid; they adduct the arytenoids and continue into the aryepiglottic folds as the sphincter of the laryngeal inlet.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Muscular process (posterior surface) of one arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the opposite arytenoid cartilage; some fibers continue as the aryepiglottic part to the epiglottis

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (laryngeal branches)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts the arytenoid cartilages, closing the intercartilaginous part of the rima glottidis; with the aryepiglottic part narrows the laryngeal inlet

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superficial (posterior) to the transverse arytenoid

cards.name: Cricopharyngeus (cricopharyngeal part of inferior pharyngeal constrictor)
cards.function: Lowest, horizontal part of the inferior constrictor that loops around the pharyngoesophageal junction as the upper esophageal sphincter; tonically closed and relaxing only as the bolus arrives.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Side of the cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Encircles the pharyngoesophageal junction to the opposite side of the cricoid without a raphe; blends below with the circular esophageal muscle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus, with branches from the recurrent laryngeal nerve

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Ascending pharyngeal artery and branches of the superior thyroid artery (with the inferior thyroid artery)

details.label: Action
details.value: Upper esophageal sphincter: tonically contracted between swallows to keep air out of the esophagus and prevent reflux; relaxes during swallowing

details.label: Gaps
details.value: Above it, between its fibers and the thyropharyngeal part: Killian dehiscence. Below it: the V-shaped area (of Laimer) of sparse longitudinal esophageal muscle. The recurrent laryngeal nerve passes deep to its lower border

cards.pearl: Failure of cricopharyngeal relaxation raises hypopharyngeal pressure and pushes mucosa out through Killian dehiscence (Zenker diverticulum); it is also the narrowest part of the gut tube, where swallowed foreign bodies lodge and endoscopes perforate.

cards.name: Superior longitudinal muscle of tongue
cards.function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running the length of the dorsum just under the mucosa; shortens the tongue and curls its tip and edges upward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Submucous fibers at the back of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the tongue; unites with the muscle of the opposite side

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens the tongue and turns the tip and sides upward

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Thin sheet immediately beneath the mucosa of the dorsum

cards.name: Inferior longitudinal muscle of tongue
cards.function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running along the under surface; shortens the tongue and curls its tip downward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Under surface of the tongue between genioglossus and hyoglossus

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the tongue, blending with styloglossus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens the tongue and turns the tip and sides downward

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Narrow band close to the inferior surface, lateral to genioglossus and medial to hyoglossus; the deep lingual artery runs along it

cards.name: Transverse muscle of tongue
cards.function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running from the midline septum to the lateral margins; narrows and lengthens the tongue.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Median fibrous septum of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Dorsum and sides of the tongue

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Narrows and elongates the tongue (with the vertical muscle, protrudes it)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Fibers interweave with the vertical muscle between the superior and inferior longitudinal muscles

cards.name: Vertical muscle of tongue
cards.function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running from the dorsum to the under surface at the borders of the forepart; flattens and widens the tongue.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Mucous membrane on the dorsum of the forepart of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Fibers extend from the dorsum to the undersurface of the tongue

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Flattens and broadens the tongue

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Confined to the borders of the forepart of the tongue; interweaves with the transverse muscle

cards.name: Rectus capitis posterior major
cards.function: Larger of the two posterior recti; extends the head and rotates it to the same side, and forms the superomedial side of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (C2)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head and rotates it to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superomedial boundary of the suboccipital triangle; lateral to rectus capitis posterior minor, deep to semispinalis capitis

cards.pearl: The suboccipital triangle it bounds contains the horizontal segment of the vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve on the posterior arch of the atlas.

cards.name: Rectus capitis posterior minor
cards.function: Small medial suboccipital muscle from the atlas to the occiput; extends the head at the atlanto-occipital joint. It is not a boundary of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Tubercle of the posterior arch of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medial and deep to rectus capitis posterior major; overlies the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane

cards.name: Obliquus capitis superior
cards.function: Suboccipital muscle from the atlas up to the occiput; extends the head and bends it to the same side, and forms the superolateral side of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse process of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head and bends it laterally

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superolateral boundary of the suboccipital triangle

cards.name: Obliquus capitis inferior
cards.function: Only suboccipital muscle that does not reach the skull; it runs from the axis to the atlas and rotates the atlas, turning the face to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (C2)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Transverse process of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Rotates the atlas (and head) to turn the face to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior boundary of the suboccipital triangle; the greater occipital nerve (C2) hooks around its lower border and ascends across it

cards.pearl: The greater occipital nerve winds around its inferior border, a landmark for nerve blocks and a site of entrapment in occipital neuralgia.

cards.name: Rectus capitis anterior
cards.function: Short prevertebral muscle from the atlas to the base of the skull, deep to longus capitis; flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior surface of the lateral mass of the atlas

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Base (basilar part) of the occipital bone in front of the foramen magnum and occipital condyle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami of C1–C2

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the vertebral artery; ascending pharyngeal artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes the head (nodding) and stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to the upper part of longus capitis; anterior to the atlanto-occipital joint

cards.name: Rectus capitis lateralis
cards.function: Short muscle from the transverse process of the atlas to the jugular process of the occipital bone; bends the head to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper surface of the transverse process of the atlas

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior surface of the jugular process of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami of C1–C2

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the vertebral artery, occipital artery and ascending pharyngeal artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes the head laterally to the same side; stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies immediately behind the internal jugular vein as it leaves the jugular foramen; the anterior ramus of C1 emerges medial to it

cards.pearl: It lies directly behind the jugular foramen and is detached in far-lateral approaches to expose the jugular bulb.

cards.name: Longissimus cervicis
cards.function: Cervical portion of the longissimus (intermediate) column of erector spinae; extends the neck and bends it to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae (T1–T5)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C6

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Bilaterally extends the cervical spine; unilaterally bends it to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral to semispinalis cervicis and medial to iliocostalis cervicis; longissimus capitis lies on its medial side; deep to splenius cervicis

cards.name: Spinalis cervicis
cards.function: Thin, inconstant cervical portion of the spinalis (medial) column of erector spinae, running between spinous processes beside the nuchal ligament; extends the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lower nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7 (and upper thoracic vertebrae)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (sometimes C3–C4)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the cervical spine

details.label: Relations
details.value: Most medial erector spinae column, alongside the nuchal ligament; often blended with semispinalis cervicis

cards.name: Multifidus (cervical part)
cards.function: Deep transversospinalis fascicles filling the groove beside the cervical spinous processes; they stabilize the cervical segments during movement.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Articular processes of C4–C7

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous processes of the vertebrae above, spanning two to four segments (up to the axis)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves (medial branches)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Stabilizes the cervical spine; assists extension and rotation to the opposite side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to semispinalis cervicis; superficial to the rotatores cervicis

cards.pearl: Multifidus atrophies with fatty infiltration after whiplash injury and in chronic neck pain, visible on MRI.

cards.name: Interspinales cervicis
cards.function: Short paired segmental muscles joining adjacent cervical spinous processes on each side of the interspinous ligament; aid extension of the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of a cervical vertebra (C3–T1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous process of the adjacent vertebra above (C2–C7)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Aid in extension of the cervical vertebral column; segmental stabilizers

details.label: Relations
details.value: Paired, one on each side of the interspinous ligament between the bifid cervical spinous processes; best developed in the neck

cards.name: Common tendinous ring (of Zinn)
cards.function: Fibrous ring at the apex of the orbit surrounding the optic canal and the medial part of the superior orbital fissure; common origin of the four rectus muscles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Periosteum of the body and lesser wing of the sphenoid around the optic canal, bridging the medial part of the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Gives origin to the superior, medial, inferior and lateral rectus muscles

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerves passing through the ring: optic nerve (CN II), superior and inferior branches of the oculomotor nerve (CN III), nasociliary nerve (CN V1), abducent nerve (CN VI)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Ophthalmic artery passes through the ring with the optic nerve in the optic canal

details.label: Action
details.value: Fixed anchor for the four recti, which form the muscular cone of the orbit

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Structures outside the ring (through the lateral part of the superior orbital fissure): lacrimal nerve, frontal nerve, trochlear nerve (CN IV), superior ophthalmic vein. Levator palpebrae superioris and superior oblique arise above and medial to the ring; inferior oblique arises from the anterior orbital floor

cards.pearl: Orbital apex syndrome: a lesion at the ring causes ophthalmoplegia (CN III, IV, VI), V1 sensory loss and visual loss (CN II); because the recti attach to the optic nerve sheath here, eye movement is painful in optic neuritis.

cards.name: Superior and inferior tarsi (tarsal plates)
cards.function: Dense fibrous plates that stiffen the eyelids, contain the tarsal (meibomian) glands, and receive the lid elevators.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior tarsus (larger, about 10 mm high; receives levator palpebrae superioris and the superior tarsal muscle); inferior tarsus (smaller, about 5 mm high; in the lower lid)

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anchored to the orbital margins by the medial and lateral palpebral ligaments; continuous peripherally with the orbital septum

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Levator palpebrae superioris inserts on the anterior surface, and the superior tarsal (Müller's) muscle on the upper edge, of the superior tarsus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Sensory: V1 branches (upper lid) and infraorbital nerve, V2 (lower lid)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Palpebral arcades from the medial and lateral palpebral arteries (ophthalmic and lacrimal arteries)

details.label: Action
details.value: Give the lids shape and firmness; tarsal glands open at the lid margin and secrete the lipid layer of the tear film

cards.pearl: A chalazion is a painless granulomatous lump from a blocked tarsal (meibomian) gland within the tarsus, in contrast to the painful stye (hordeolum) of a lash follicle gland at the lid margin.

cards.name: Temporal fascia
cards.function: Strong fascial sheet covering temporalis from the superior temporal line to the zygomatic arch; gives origin to the superficial fibers of the muscle.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superficial layer (attaches to the lateral margin of the upper border of the zygomatic arch); deep layer (attaches to the medial margin); a fat pad lies between them above the arch

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior temporal line of the frontal and parietal bones

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper border of the zygomatic arch, after splitting into superficial and deep layers

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Not applicable (overlying skin: auriculotemporal and zygomaticotemporal nerves)

details.label: Action
details.value: Roofs the temporal fossa and gives origin to temporalis; resists the downward pull of masseter on the zygomatic arch

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle temporal artery (from superficial temporal artery) pierces it; superficial temporal vessels lie on its surface

cards.pearl: The temporal branch of the facial nerve crosses the zygomatic arch superficial to this fascia, so surgeons elevate flaps deep to its superficial layer to protect the nerve (Gillies approach to a depressed zygomatic arch runs beneath it).

cards.name: Superficial (investing) layer of deep cervical fascia
cards.function: Outermost layer of deep cervical fascia, encircling the whole neck deep to platysma and splitting to enclose sternocleidomastoid and trapezius; it roofs the anterior and posterior triangles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Above: superior nuchal line, mastoid process, zygomatic arch, lower border of the mandible and hyoid bone; behind: nuchal ligament and cervical spinous processes

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Below: manubrium, clavicle, acromion and spine of scapula; above the manubrium it splits to enclose the suprasternal space (of Burns)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pierced by the cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus at the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: External and anterior jugular veins run on or pierce it

details.label: Action
details.value: Encloses and compartmentalizes the neck; limits the superficial spread of infection

details.label: Relations
details.value: Splits to enclose sternocleidomastoid and trapezius and the submandibular and parotid glands (parotid and masseteric fascia); the pretracheal layer, carotid sheath and prevertebral layer lie deep to it

cards.pearl: The accessory nerve crosses the posterior triangle just deep to this layer, so it is at risk in lymph node biopsy; the external jugular vein pierces the fascia above the clavicle and is held open there, permitting air embolism if cut.
